content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now. The main facts are that metrics stopped at 19:10, right after deploy P2 renamed the metrics port from "metrics" to "http-metrics," and I'm checking how the scrape config matches targets against that port name.

I'm checking whether the mechanism in the root cause depends on a reading I haven't actually verified, since the scrape config's port name only shows up in one file. The config comment and the rollback that restored the old name seem to cover it, so I'm weighing whether that's enough.

I'm checking the logs next: the ClientDisconnected errors went from about 2 a minute to 1.5 a minute, and the error rate is typically lower after the deploy, peaking slightly higher at 19:15. That looks like normal client noise, so I'd call serving unchanged.

I'm laying out the causal chain now: first that the shop's metrics stopped arriving from 19:10 even though nobody using the shop noticed, and then that the scraper had no target matching the renamed port.

I'm ruling out the earlier deploy P1 as the cause, since metrics were still being collected until 19:09 with P1 already in place. The rollback to P1's revision also confirmed that the rename in P2 is what broke collection.

I'm checking the rollback step now: P1's revision was restored and metrics came back, so the earlier deploy is ruled out, and no flag changes showed up in the window. Next I'm working out why the rename broke collection: the scrape config selects its target by port name, and since scrape.yaml was unchanged and still selected `metrics`, nothing matched `http-metrics`, so the scraper quietly stopped collecting.

I'm settling on the root cause now: the scrape config selects the shop's metrics endpoint by port name, and the deploy renamed that port from `metrics` to `http-metrics`, so nothing matched and the scraper silently stopped collecting.

I'm weighing whether the contributing-factor claim holds: nothing checks that the port name in values-production.yaml matches the name the scrape config selects, and no such check appears before the change shipped. A check in CI on every deploy/ change would have caught the rename, so that's the item I'm considering for the fix.

I'm weighing a fix for the contributing factor: a check on whether the port name in values-production.yaml matches what the scrape config selects, run in the deploy pipeline so a mismatch blocks the deploy. I'm also considering an alert on the scrape target count, since a selector matching no endpoint fails silently and the absence alert only caught it after several minutes.

I'm weighing whether the missing paging is a contributing factor, since nobody was paged for the silent metrics gap. It held before the incident and didn't extend the outage, so I'm leaning toward recording it as a finding, with an action item to route the MetricsAbsent alert for the shop to on-call.

I'm weighing whether to note that nobody was paged, since the MetricsAbsent alert didn't reach on-call. I'll record that under what went wrong, with an action item to route it, though it didn't prolong the outage. I'm also considering a second contributing factor: the scraper reports nothing when a selector matches no port, so only the vanishing series revealed it, and an alert on a zero-target scrape config would have named the cause directly.

I'm checking the still-at-risk part now: the repository still holds the renamed port at 9f4ad14 while the scrape config selects the old name, so any later sync or deploy from it could stop the metrics being collected again without anyone noticing until the series disappears.

I'm drafting the action items now: a deploy-pipeline check that the port name in the scrape configuration matches what the chart sets, an alert for when the shop's scrape configuration matches no target, and routing the MetricsAbsent alert to on-call so someone gets paged. I'm also noting that the repository still holds the renamed port, so any sync or future one-file rename could stop the shop's metrics again.

I'm checking what the investigation found next: metrics resumed after the rollback, which confirms the fix, and the flag provider history shows no flag changes around the time of the incident. I'm noting that nobody got paged for the silent gap, and that the alert came later than the timeline accounts for, though I'm leaving the timing aside. I'm also weighing whether anything was lucky here, and I'm leaning toward recording none.

I'm settling the cause-in-plain-words line: it should say a configuration change renamed the port label monitoring uses to find the shop's metrics, without the monitoring setting being updated to match, so collection stopped. I'm dropping the clause about the shop still working, since that's covered elsewhere, and keeping the wording free of figures and specific times.

I'm checking the timing of the deploy against the root-cause write-up: P2 is dated by its own row, at the moment it rolled out, and I'm making sure the postmortem cites that instant rather than a loose window.

action_items.item: Make the deploy pipeline check, on every change to the deploy/ directory, that every port name the scrape configuration selects equals metrics.portName in values-production.yaml, and block the deploy when they differ.
Add an alert that fires when io-shop's scrape configuration matches no scrape target.
Route MetricsAbsent alerts on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged.

causal_chain.step: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. What was seen instead: the shop's metrics stopped arriving, and the MetricsAbsent alert fired on the missing series.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 of revision e283ba3af732fc4285166a060b827b1305cd30d9. Metrics were collected with it in place up to the minute before the onset. The rollback put that revision back, was confirmed, and the metrics resumed.
A feature flag change. The flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour read.

causal_chain.step: The metrics stopped because of deploy P2 of revision 9f4ad14582c99c497eb6c2d2af87566cd4493020 at {P2.1}. It changed one value, metrics.portName in deploy/values-production.yaml, from `metrics` to `http-metrics`, and changed no other file.

The rename broke collection because the scraper chooses its target by the port's name. The scrape configuration, which the deploy left untouched, still selected the old name. No port matched it, so the scraper quietly stopped collecting while the shop went on publishing.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change renamed the label that the monitoring system uses to find where the shop publishes its figures, but the monitoring's own setting was not changed to match, so the monitoring could no longer find the figures and stopped collecting them.

contributing_factors.factor: Nothing checked that the port name in values-production.yaml matched the name the scrape configuration selects. The file's own comment calls the name load-bearing, and no check was seen catching the mismatch before the change went out.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check comparing the two names would have failed on the rename, and the deploy would have been stopped before the scraper lost its target.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: When a selector matches no port, the scraper reports no error. The fault was found only by the MetricsAbsent alert on the missing series.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An alert on a scrape selector matching no target would have pointed straight at the mismatched name as soon as the scraper lost the target, instead of waiting for the series to be absent.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read the deployment's diff and found that one configuration value, the metrics port's name, had changed.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone but Argus.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop. The action can be undone.
The Mitigation Agent saw the metrics could be read again and judged the rollback confirmed.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix and a test as draft pull request #443 for a person to review.

went_wrong: The MetricsAbsent alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.

input.root_cause: The scrape configuration picks the shop's metrics endpoint by the port's name, not its number. The deploy renamed the port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` in values-production.yaml and left the scrape configuration unchanged, still selecting `metrics`. With no port left carrying that name, the scraper had no target and quietly stopped collecting, while the shop went on publishing on the same endpoint.
input.still_at_risk: Deploying the repository as it stands, or any later rename of the port in only one of the two files, could stop the shop's metrics being collected again, and nobody would be told until the series went missing.
input.symptom: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong; instead, the shop's metrics stopped being collected
